newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Lib Dems seen leading in Slovenia election - poll.
newsitem.headline: Lib Dems seen leading in Slovenia election - poll.

text.p: Slovenia's ruling Liberal Democrats of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek were forecast on Sunday to emerge as the biggest party in a general election, according to exit polls.

Results of the exit polls released by PopTV just minutes after polling stations closed at 7 p.m. (1800 GMT) showed Dronvsek's party ahead with 28.1 percent of the vote, up from 23.46 percent in the last election in 1992.

The centre-right Social Democrats led by former defence minister Janez Jansa, were estimated to have won 18.6 percent, with the rightist People's Party in third place with 18.1 percent, the exit polls showed.
If translated into concrete results, the figures would mark a large rise in support for the Social Democrats, who won 3.3 percent in the last general election.

The Christian Democrats, the Liberal Democrats' junior coalition partner, took fourth position with 8.7 percent, closely followed by the former communist United List of Social Democrats with 8.6 percent, according to the polls.
Desus, a party representing pensioners, had 3.7 percent, ahead of the Slovenian Nationalist Party on 3.6 percent.

Drnovsek was battling a loose alliance of rightwing parties which include the Social Democrats, the People's Party and Christian Democrats. Their combined vote was forecast at 45.4 percent, which would put them in a position to challenge the ruling parties' leadership.
Drnovsek, a firm backer of European Union and NATO membership, could be forced to form a coalition with one or more rightwing parties if he wants to form the ex-Yugoslav republic's new government.
